compiled_state.title: As a sprint orchestrator, Phase A opens a long-lived draft PR and the merge-to-main-pr.sh guard refuses only non-draft duplicates
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Phase A opens a draft PR from the session branch to main via `gh pr create --draft`, completing before any story-branch dispatch in Phase E. The merge-to-main-pr.sh existing 'refuse if open PR exists' guard is amended to 'refuse if non-draft PR exists' so the long-lived draft pattern is supported. Subsumes 1083-fb3d's PR-creation scope.
**Why**: Provides the durable PR substrate that GitHubPRDefenseStore (S8/S10) keys on from sprint start, eliminating the non-PR-keying gap.

**Scope**:
- IN: Phase A: gh pr create --draft from session branch to main; PR creation completes before Phase E dispatch
- IN: merge-to-main-pr.sh guard amended to non-draft-only
- IN: PR title/body templated with epic ID + sprint session ID
- OUT: CI workflow trigger on push to story/* — owned by S8
- OUT: DefenseStore activation logic — owned by S8

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, post-Phase-A, gh pr list returns one draft PR with the session branch as head and main as base
  ← Satisfies: "SC5: Long-lived draft PR + per-story CI review"
- When this story is complete, an attempt to invoke merge-to-main-pr.sh while a draft PR is open succeeds (creates or updates the PR); an attempt while a non-draft PR is open is refused with the documented error
  ← Satisfies: "SC5: guard amendment to refuse if non-draft PR exists"
- When this story is complete, Phase A blocks Phase E dispatch until PR creation completes
  ← Satisfies: "SC5: Phase A is a blocking step"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] The amended guard must distinguish (a) a sprint-active draft PR from this epic, (b) a stale draft PR from a previous abandoned sprint, and (c) a release-pipeline non-draft PR opened by merge-to-main.sh itself. Define positive and negative cases with explicit tests for each. Without this distinction, the guard may block legitimate release pipelines or allow duplicate sprint draft PRs.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
